title: Too Smart for Your Own Good
style: Dark dubstep, layered vocals with melodic soprano verses in crooning legato phrasing, whispered ad-libs between lines, bass baritone vocals in drops and bridge; heavy half-time groove; sidechain-pumped bass layers and a dry bridge build; heavy electronic synth stabs, sparse sub-bass lead and glitch clicks, ending on residual high noise and a distant alarm tone.
lyrics:
[Intro – sparse sub-bass, glitch clicks]
Keep an organizer
Scratch notes to yourself
Set the alarms on repeat
Do it enough, the habit takes hold

[Pre-Drop]
But the habit of building habits
Is a habit that quietly folds

[Drop]
You’re too smart for your own good
Every fix has an exit route
Too smart for your own good
You crack the codes and then refuse

[Verse 1]
They say hack the system
Gamify the climb
You thrive on the novelty
Then choke when the novelty dies

So rebrand the duty
Dress it up as bliss
Still the mind finds the loophole
Still the mind slips the fist

[Drop]
You’re too smart for your own good
Every fix has an exit route
Too smart for your own good
You crack the codes and then refuse

[Verse 2]
Tell someone, make it public
Turn the promise into debt
So better stay silent
Fail alone than fail in debt

The quiet collapse feels cleaner
Than the noise of being caught
You watch the pattern unravel
And call the watching “thought”

[Bridge – half-time, dry, rising pressure]
Too aware to fool yourself
Too asocial to use
The fear of letting people down
As fuel you refuse

No outside shame
No borrowed chain
Just the private loop
Of knowing better… and staying the same

[Final Drop / Outro]
You’re too smart for your own good
Too aware to trick the game
Too smart for your own good
You fail in silence
And wear it like a name

[bass drops out → residual high noise + distant alarm tone]
